section_1.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that the same physical point in space can be described by different sets of coordinates depending on the observer's 'grid' (basis). Use a relatable scenario to establish the 'Why'.
section_1.example: An explorer (Character A) uses a standard North-East grid, while a Pirate (Character B) uses a grid aligned with their tilted treasure map. They are both looking at the same 'X' marks the spot, but their coordinate values are different.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Vector
section_2.content: Briefly refresh the idea that a vector is a 'recipe' of basis vectors. In the standard basis (i, j), the vector [3, 2] means '3 steps of i and 2 steps of j'. Focus on the visual of scaling and adding arrows.
section_2.example: An animation showing a robot moving 3 units along the x-axis and 2 units along the y-axis to reach a target.

section_3.title: Visualizing a New Basis
section_3.content: Introduce a 'New Basis' (B) consisting of two vectors, b1 and b2, that aren't perpendicular or unit-length. Show how a new grid forms from these vectors. Emphasize that the space hasn't changed, only the ruler we use to measure it.
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'Squashed and Rotated' grid overlaid on the standard Cartesian plane. A vector that was [1, 1] in the standard grid might only be [0.5, 0] in this new, stretched grid.

section_4.title: The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix
section_4.content: Explain how to bridge the two worlds. The 'Change of Basis Matrix' (P) is simply a matrix where the columns are the coordinates of the NEW basis vectors (b1, b2) written in terms of the OLD basis.
section_4.example: If the Pirate's first basis vector is [2, 1] in our standard view, and their second is [-1, 1], the transition matrix P is [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. This matrix 'speaks' both languages.

section_5.title: The Mathematical Transformation
section_5.content: Present the formula: [v]_standard = P * [v]_new. Explain that multiplying the Pirate's coordinates by matrix P 'translates' them back into our standard language. Mention that P-inverse does the opposite.
section_5.example: The Pirate says the treasure is at [1, 1] on his map. We multiply P * [1, 1] to find that in our standard grid, the treasure is actually at [2-1, 1+1] = [1, 2].

section_6.title: Summary & Global View
section_6.content: Recap the flow: Basis -> Grid -> Matrix -> Translation. Highlight that change of basis is the foundation for complex operations like Diagonalization and Image Compression.
section_6.example: A final animation showing the grid 'morphing' from the Pirate's perspective back to the standard perspective, with the vector arrow staying fixed in space while the numbers change.

lecture_lines: Let's define a new basis using vectors b1 and b2.
These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.
The space remains fixed while our ruler changes.
animations: Show a dim grey (#696969) standard grid in the background.
Introduce basis vectors b1 (orange, #FFA500) and b2 (cyan, #00FFFF) starting from origin.
Generate a new skewed grid using orange (#FFA500) and cyan (#00FFFF) lines.

section_4.title: The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix
lecture_lines: Matrix P bridges these two different coordinate worlds.
Its columns are new basis vectors in standard terms.
This matrix serves as a translation manual between grids.
animations: Display standard basis vectors i (#0000FF) and j (#00FF00) as reference.
Plot Pirate's basis vectors b1 (#FFA500) at [2, 1] and b2 (#00FFFF) at [-1, 1].
Highlight the standard coordinates of b1 and b2 with dashed lines.
Form matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] by placing b1 and b2 as columns.
Label the columns of P as 'b1' and 'b2' in their respective colors.

section_5.title: The Mathematical Transformation
lecture_lines: We translate new coordinates using matrix multiplication.
Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.
P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.
The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.
This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned.
animations: Display formula [v]_std = P * [v]_new in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Show the Pirate's vector [1, 1] in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the formula.
Substitute matrix P and vector [1, 1] into the matrix multiplication.
Calculate the product: [2*1 + -1*1, 1*1 + 1*1] resulting in [1, 2].
Highlight the resulting vector [1, 2] on the standard grid in white (#FFFFFF).

section_6.title: Summary & Global View
lecture_lines: Change of basis maps grids to different perspectives.
It is the foundation for diagonalization and compression.
One vector, many views: that is change of basis.
animations: Display a sequence: Basis -> Grid -> Matrix -> Translation in white (#FFFFFF).
Morph the tilted grid back to standard while the vector arrow remains fixed.
Display 'Diagonalization' and 'Compression' as key applications in green (#00FF00).

outline.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
outline.content: Introduce the concept that the same physical point in space can be described by different sets of coordinates depending on the observer's 'grid' (basis). Use a relatable scenario to establish the 'Why'.
outline.example: An explorer (Character A) uses a standard North-East grid, while a Pirate (Character B) uses a grid aligned with their tilted treasure map. They are both looking at the same 'X' marks the spot, but their coordinate values are different.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
lecture_lines: One point can have many different coordinate descriptions.
An explorer uses a standard North-East grid.
A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid.
They see the same "X" using different numbers.
Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis.
animations: Draw a standard white (#FFFFFF) grid with a red 'X' (#FF0000) at (3, 2).

Highlight the red 'X' (#FF0000) position relative to the Pirate's yellow grid lines.
Add labels: Standard [3, 2] in white (#FFFFFF) and Pirate [v1, v2] in yellow (#FFFF00).

outline.content: Present the formula: [v]_standard = P * [v]_new. Explain that multiplying the Pirate's coordinates by matrix P 'translates' them back into our standard language. Mention that P-inverse does the opposite.
outline.example: The Pirate says the treasure is at [1, 1] on his map. We multiply P * [1, 1] to find that in our standard grid, the treasure is actually at [2-1, 1+1] = [1, 2].

Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.
P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.
The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.
This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned.

Show the Pirate's vector [1, 1] in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the formula.
Substitute matrix P and vector [1, 1] into the matrix multiplication.
Calculate the product: [2*1 + -1*1, 1*1 + 1*1] resulting in [1, 2].
Highlight the resulting vector [1, 2] on the standard grid in white (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Visualizing a New Basis"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Let's define a new basis using vectors b1 and b2.",
            "- These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.",
            "- The space remains fixed while our ruler changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from the prompt/storyboard
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        GREY = "#696969"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color the first lecture line to match b1/b2 theme
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # 1. Dim grey (#696969) standard grid background.
        # We use a NumberPlane to represent the standard Cartesian ruler.
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GREY}
        )
        # Position in columns 2-6 to respect margin (B021)
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        origin = std_grid.get_origin()
        
        self.play(Create(std_grid))
        
        # 2. Basis vectors b1 (orange #FFA500), b2 (cyan #00FFFF) from origin.
        # Basis B defined as b1=[1.5, 0.5] and b2=[0.5, 1.5]
        b1_coords = np.array([1.5, 0.5, 0])
        b2_coords = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        
        b1_arrow = Arrow(origin, std_grid.coords_to_point(b1_coords[0], b1_coords[1]), buff=0, color=ORANGE)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(origin, std_grid.coords_to_point(b2_coords[0], b2_coords[1]), buff=0, color=CYAN)
        
        # Labels for basis vectors (B001, B002 context)
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1", color=ORANGE).scale(0.8)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2", color=CYAN).scale(0.8)
        
        # Position labels at the end of arrows with a small offset
        b1_label.next_to(b1_arrow.get_end(), RIGHT + DOWN, buff=0.1)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT + UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_arrow), Write(b1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b2_arrow), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color transition for the second line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 3. New skewed grid using orange and cyan lines.
        # This grid represents the "squashed and rotated" coordinate system.
        matrix = [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]] # The transformation defined by the basis vectors
        
        skewed_grid = VGroup()
        # Vertical lines (transformed unit x steps)
        for x in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([x, -3, 0]), np.array([x, 3, 0]), color=ORANGE, stroke_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
        # Horizontal lines (transformed unit y steps)
        for y in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([-3, y, 0]), np.array( [3, y, 0]), color=CYAN, stroke_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
            
        # Apply the basis transformation
        skewed_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        # Move the skewed grid to align its origin with the standard grid origin
        # Note: apply_matrix happens relative to the VGroup center, which is origin (0,0,0)
        # We need to move it to the 'origin' we calculated for the std_grid.
        # self.place_in_area would center the bounding box, which works here since the grid is symmetric.
        self.place_in_area(skewed_grid, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The space remains fixed while our ruler changes."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # To illustrate the fixed space, we show a constant vector v = [2, 2] in std coordinates.
        # In the new basis [1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5], this vector is exactly 1*b1 + 1*b2
        v_coords_std = [2, 2]
        v_arrow = Arrow(origin, std_grid.coords_to_point(*v_coords_std), buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).scale(0.9)
        v_label.next_to(v_arrow.get_end(), UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Highlighting the vector against the two overlapping grids
        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_arrow, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix"
        lines = [
            "Matrix P bridges these two different coordinate worlds.",
            "Its columns are new basis vectors in standard terms.",
            "This matrix serves as a translation manual between grids."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_B1 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_B2 = "#00FFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Axes for the vectors
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C},
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'F4')
        
        # Standard basis vectors
        vec_i = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_I)
        vec_j = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_J)
        
        lbl_i = MathTex("i", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20).next_to(vec_i.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        lbl_j = MathTex("j", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20).next_to(vec_j.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Pirate basis vectors
        vec_b1 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_B1)
        vec_b2 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_B2)
        
        lbl_b1 = MathTex("b_1", color=COLOR_B1, font_size=20).next_to(vec_b1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        lbl_b2 = MathTex("b_2", color=COLOR_B2, font_size=20).next_to(vec_b2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(vec_i), Create(vec_j), Write(lbl_i), Write(lbl_j))
        self.play(Create(vec_b1), Create(vec_b2), Write(lbl_b1), Write(lbl_b2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dashed lines for b1 standard coordinates (2, 1)
        dash_b1_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(2, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), color=COLOR_B1)
        dash_b1_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(2, 1), color=COLOR_B1)
        
        # Dashed lines for b2 standard coordinates (-1, 1)
        dash_b2_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(-1, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), color=COLOR_B2)
        dash_b2_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(-1, 1), color=COLOR_B2)
        
        self.play(Create(dash_b1_x), Create(dash_b1_y))
        self.play(Create(dash_b2_x), Create(dash_b2_y))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Matrix P construction
        # Matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        matrix_p = Matrix(
            [[2, -1], [1, 1]],
            left_bracket="[",
            right_bracket="]",
            element_to_mobject_config={"font_size": 28}
        )
        # Color columns
        matrix_p.get_columns()[0].set_color(COLOR_B1)
        matrix_p.get_columns()[1].set_color(COLOR_B2)
        
        # Matrix Label
        p_label = MathTex("P = ", font_size=28)
        p_group = VGroup(p_label, matrix_p).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Column labels
        b1_col_lbl = MathTex("b_1", color=COLOR_B1, font_size=20)
        b2_col_lbl = MathTex("b_2", color=COLOR_B2, font_size=20)
        
        # Use B002 to center the matrix group
        self.place_in_area(p_group, 'B5', 'D6', scale_factor=0.9)
        # Anchor column labels relative to the matrix
        b1_col_lbl.next_to(matrix_p.get_columns()[0], UP, buff=0.2)
        b2_col_lbl.next_to(matrix_p.get_columns()[1], UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(p_group))
        self.play(Write(b1_col_lbl), Write(b2_col_lbl))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "We translate new coordinates using matrix multiplication.",
            "Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.",
            "P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.",
            "The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.",
            "This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We translate new coordinates using matrix multiplication.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        formula = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{std} = P \cdot [\vec{v}]_{new}", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        matrix_p_def = MathTex(r"P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_p_def, 'C1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_p_def, shift=UP*0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        p_inv_text = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{new} = P^{-1} \cdot [\vec{v}]_{std}", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(p_inv_text, 'D1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(p_inv_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Transition: Remove P-inverse and P def to make room for substitution
        self.play(FadeOut(p_inv_text), FadeOut(matrix_p_def))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        v_new_pirate = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{new} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=YELLOW_COLOR)

        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, substitution[0]))
        self.play(FadeIn(substitution[1:]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        # Calculation: [2*1 - 1*1; 1*1 + 1*1] = [1; 2]
        result_vec_math = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{std} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(result_vec_math, 'D1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Transform(substitution, result_vec_math))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show grid and highlight [1, 2]

        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},

        # Wrap in VGroup to use grid system

        self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        v_std_arrow = Arrow(
            start=grid.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=grid.coords_to_point(1, 2),
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE_COLOR
        )
        v_std_label = MathTex(r"[1, 2]", color=WHITE_COLOR, font_size=20)
        v_std_label.next_to(v_std_arrow.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(grid), 
            FadeOut(v_new_pirate), 
            substitution.animate.scale(0.8).move_to(self.grid['C4'])
        )
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_std_arrow), Write(v_std_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Vector", 
                          ["A vector is a recipe of basis vectors.", 
                           "Vector [3, 2] means 3 i-steps and 2 j-steps.", 
                           "We reach the target by scaling and adding arrows."])
        
        # Global Colors
        color_i = "#0000FF" # blue
        color_j = "#00FF00" # green
        color_result = "#800080" # purple

        # Origin for our vector space (centered on grid)
        origin_pos = self.grid['D2']

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw standard unit vectors i (blue) and j (green) at the origin.
        
        # i vector: D2 -> D3
        i_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['D3'], buff=0, color=color_i)
        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color=color_i, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0) # Positioned below the tip
        
        # j vector: D2 -> C2
        j_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['C2'], buff=0, color=color_j)
        j_label = MathTex("\\hat{j}", color=color_j, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C1', scale_factor=1.0) # Positioned to the left of tip
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Create(i_vec), 
            Create(j_vec), 
            Write(i_label), 
            Write(j_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a robot icon moving 3 units along i, then 2 units along j.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Asset: Robot [Asset: Robot/robot.png]
        robot = ImageMobject("Robot/robot.png")
        robot.scale(0.3)
        robot.move_to(origin_pos)
        self.add(robot)
        
        # Path sequence:
        # Move along x: D2 -> D3 -> D4 -> D5
        # Move along y: D5 -> C5 -> B5
        move_targets = ['D3', 'D4', 'D5', 'C5', 'B5']
        
        for target in move_targets:
            self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid[target]), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
            
        # Draw component vectors (scaled basis vectors)
        i_scaled = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['D5'], buff=0, color=color_i, stroke_width=2)
        j_scaled = Arrow(start=self.grid['D5'], end=self.grid['B5'], buff=0, color=color_j, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(i_scaled), Create(j_scaled))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw the resulting vector [3, 2] from origin to the robot's position in purple.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_result))
        
        res_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['B5'], buff=0, color=color_result, stroke_width=6)
        res_label = MathTex("\\vec{v} = \\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\\\ 2 \\end{bmatrix}", color=color_result, font_size=32)
        # B6 is near the tip B5
        self.place_at_grid(res_label, 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(res_vec), Write(res_label))
        self.wait(3)

        vector_label = Text("v", font_size=18, color=PURPLE).next_to(vector_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Morphing sequence
        self.play(FadeIn(pirate_grid))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_arrow), FadeIn(vector_label))

        # Morph grid back to standard while vector stays fixed
        self.play(
            Transform(pirate_grid, std_grid),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )

        c1, c2 = 2.65, 0.61 # Derived coefficients for (3,2) in Pirate basis
        
        pirate_proj_1 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c1*p_b1, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        pirate_proj_2 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c2*p_b2, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        self.play(Create(std_proj_x), Create(std_proj_y))
        self.play(Create(pirate_proj_1), Create(pirate_proj_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        std_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Standard: } \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        pirate_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Pirate: } \begin{bmatrix} 2.65 \\ 0.61 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        # Place labels in footer area of the grid
        self.place_in_area(std_coords, 'F1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(pirate_coords, 'F4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Write(std_coords), Write(pirate_coords))
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that the same physical point in space can be described by different sets of coordinates depending on the observer's 'grid' (basis). Use a relatable scenario to establish the 'Why'.
section_1.example: An explorer (Character A) uses a standard North-East grid, while a Pirate (Character B) uses a grid aligned with their tilted treasure map. They are both looking at the same 'X' marks the spot, but their coordinate values are different.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Vector
section_2.content: Briefly refresh the idea that a vector is a 'recipe' of basis vectors. In the standard basis (i, j), the vector [3, 2] means '3 steps of i and 2 steps of j'. Focus on the visual of scaling and adding arrows.
section_2.example: An animation showing a robot moving 3 units along the x-axis and 2 units along the y-axis to reach a target.

section_3.title: Visualizing a New Basis
section_3.content: Introduce a 'New Basis' (B) consisting of two vectors, b1 and b2, that aren't perpendicular or unit-length. Show how a new grid forms from these vectors. Emphasize that the space hasn't changed, only the ruler we use to measure it.
section_3.example: Visualizing a 'Squashed and Rotated' grid overlaid on the standard Cartesian plane. A vector that was [1, 1] in the standard grid might only be [0.5, 0] in this new, stretched grid.

section_4.title: The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix
section_4.content: Explain how to bridge the two worlds. The 'Change of Basis Matrix' (P) is simply a matrix where the columns are the coordinates of the NEW basis vectors (b1, b2) written in terms of the OLD basis.
section_4.example: If the Pirate's first basis vector is [2, 1] in our standard view, and their second is [-1, 1], the transition matrix P is [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. This matrix 'speaks' both languages.

section_5.title: The Mathematical Transformation
section_5.content: Present the formula: [v]_standard = P * [v]_new. Explain that multiplying the Pirate's coordinates by matrix P 'translates' them back into our standard language. Mention that P-inverse does the opposite.
section_5.example: The Pirate says the treasure is at [1, 1] on his map. We multiply P * [1, 1] to find that in our standard grid, the treasure is actually at [2-1, 1+1] = [1, 2].

section_6.title: Summary & Global View
section_6.content: Recap the flow: Basis -> Grid -> Matrix -> Translation. Highlight that change of basis is the foundation for complex operations like Diagonalization and Image Compression.
section_6.example: A final animation showing the grid 'morphing' from the Pirate's perspective back to the standard perspective, with the vector arrow staying fixed in space while the numbers change.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Vector", 
                          ["A vector is a recipe of basis vectors.", 
                           "Vector [3, 2] means 3 i-steps and 2 j-steps.", 
                           "We reach the target by scaling and adding arrows."])
        
        # Global Colors
        color_i = "#0000FF" # blue
        color_j = "#00FF00" # green
        color_result = "#800080" # purple

        # Origin for our vector space (centered on grid)
        origin_pos = self.grid['D2']

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw standard unit vectors i (blue) and j (green) at the origin.
        
        # i vector: D2 -> D3
        i_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['D3'], buff=0, color=color_i)
        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color=color_i, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0) # Positioned below the tip
        
        # j vector: D2 -> C2
        j_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['C2'], buff=0, color=color_j)
        j_label = MathTex("\\hat{j}", color=color_j, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C1', scale_factor=1.0) # Positioned to the left of tip
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Create(i_vec), 
            Create(j_vec), 
            Write(i_label), 
            Write(j_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a robot icon moving 3 units along i, then 2 units along j.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Asset: Robot placeholder due to missing file
        robot = Circle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        robot.scale(0.3)
        robot.move_to(origin_pos)
        self.add(robot)
        
        # Path sequence:
        # Move along x: D2 -> D3 -> D4 -> D5
        # Move along y: D5 -> C5 -> B5
        move_targets = ['D3', 'D4', 'D5', 'C5', 'B5']
        
        for target in move_targets:
            self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid[target]), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
            
        # Draw component vectors (scaled basis vectors)
        i_scaled = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['D5'], buff=0, color=color_i, stroke_width=2)
        j_scaled = Arrow(start=self.grid['D5'], end=self.grid['B5'], buff=0, color=color_j, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(i_scaled), Create(j_scaled))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw the resulting vector [3, 2] from origin to the robot's position in purple.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_result))
        
        res_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pos, end=self.grid['B5'], buff=0, color=color_result, stroke_width=6)
        res_label = MathTex("\\vec{v} = \\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\\\ 2 \\end{bmatrix}", color=color_result, font_size=32)
        # B6 is near the tip B5
        self.place_at_grid(res_label, 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(res_vec), Write(res_label))
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
outline.content: Introduce the concept that the same physical point in space can be described by different sets of coordinates depending on the observer's 'grid' (basis). Use a relatable scenario to establish the 'Why'.
outline.example: An explorer (Character A) uses a standard North-East grid, while a Pirate (Character B) uses a grid aligned with their tilted treasure map. They are both looking at the same 'X' marks the spot, but their coordinate values are different.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Perspective Problem
lecture_lines: One point can have many different coordinate descriptions.
An explorer uses a standard North-East grid.
A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid.
They see the same "X" using different numbers.
Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis.
animations: Draw a standard white (#FFFFFF) grid with a red 'X' (#FF0000) at (3, 2).
Introduce character 'Explorer' on the left side associated with the standard grid.
Overlay a tilted and stretched yellow (#FFFF00) grid representing the 'Pirate's' map.
Highlight the red 'X' (#FF0000) position relative to the Pirate's yellow grid lines.
Add labels: Standard [3, 2] in white (#FFFFFF) and Pirate [v1, v2] in yellow (#FFFF00).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Introduction: The Perspective Problem"
        lines = [
            "One point can have many different coordinate descriptions.",
            "An explorer uses a standard North-East grid.",
            "A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid.",
            "They see the same \"X\" using different numbers.",
            "Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_STANDARD = WHITE
        COLOR_PIRATE = YELLOW
        COLOR_X = RED
        
        # Core positions in the 6x6 system
        origin_pos = self.grid['D2']
        x_pos = self.grid['B5']  # Point "X" at (3, 2) relative to D2
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "One point can have many different coordinate descriptions."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        
        # Draw a red 'X'
        point_x = Cross(stroke_width=6).scale(0.2).set_color(COLOR_X)
        point_x.move_to(x_pos)
        point_x.set_z_index(10)
        
        self.play(Create(point_x))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "An explorer uses a standard North-East grid."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_STANDARD))
        
        # Standard white grid
        # x_range from -1 to 5, y_range from -1 to 4 ensures origin (0,0) is shifted
        # x_length and y_length match the number of units in range (1 unit per grid cell)
        standard_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_STANDARD, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": COLOR_STANDARD, "stroke_width": 2},
            x_length=6,
            y_length=5
        )
        # Shift origin to D2
        standard_grid.shift(origin_pos - standard_grid.get_origin())
        
        explorer_label = Text("Explorer", font_size=24, color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        self.place_at_grid(explorer_label, 'A1', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(standard_grid), Write(explorer_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PIRATE))
        
        # Tilted yellow grid
        pirate_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_PIRATE, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": COLOR_PIRATE, "stroke_width": 2},
            x_length=6,
            y_length=5
        )
        # Transformation matrix: tilted and stretched
        matrix = [[1.2, -0.3], [0.5, 1.1]]
        pirate_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        # Shift origin to D2
        pirate_grid.shift(origin_pos - pirate_grid.get_origin())
        
        pirate_label = Text("Pirate", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        self.place_at_grid(pirate_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(pirate_grid), Write(pirate_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "They see the same \"X\" using different numbers."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        
        # Standard projection lines (Horizontal/Vertical)
        std_proj_x = DashedLine(x_pos, [x_pos[0], origin_pos[1], 0], color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        std_proj_y = DashedLine(x_pos, [origin_pos[0], x_pos[1], 0], color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        
        # Pirate projection lines (Along basis vectors)
        # Basis vectors: b1 = [1.2, 0.5], b2 = [-0.3, 1.1]
        p_b1 = np.array([1.2, 0.5, 0])
        p_b2 = np.array([-0.3, 1.1, 0])
        c1, c2 = 2.65, 0.61 # Derived coefficients for (3,2) in Pirate basis
        
        pirate_proj_1 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c1*p_b1, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        pirate_proj_2 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c2*p_b2, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        self.play(Create(std_proj_x), Create(std_proj_y))
        self.play(Create(pirate_proj_1), Create(pirate_proj_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        std_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Standard: } \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        pirate_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Pirate: } \begin{bmatrix} 2.65 \\ 0.61 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        # Place labels in footer area of the grid
        self.place_in_area(std_coords, 'F1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(pirate_coords, 'F4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Write(std_coords), Write(pirate_coords))
        self.wait(2)

            "- These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from the prompt/storyboard
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"

            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GREY}

        # Position in columns 2-6 to respect margin (B021)
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        origin = std_grid.get_origin()
        
        self.play(Create(std_grid))
        
        # 2. Basis vectors b1 (orange #FFA500), b2 (cyan #00FFFF) from origin.
        # Basis B defined as b1=[1.5, 0.5] and b2=[0.5, 1.5]
        b1_coords = np.array([1.5, 0.5, 0])
        b2_coords = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        
        b1_arrow = Arrow(origin, std_grid.coords_to_point(b1_coords[0], b1_coords[1]), buff=0, color=ORANGE)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(origin, std_grid.coords_to_point(b2_coords[0], b2_coords[1]), buff=0, color=CYAN)
        
        # Labels for basis vectors (B001, B002 context)

        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2", color=CYAN).scale(0.8)

        b1_label.next_to(b1_arrow.get_end(), RIGHT + DOWN, buff=0.1)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT + UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_arrow), Write(b1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b2_arrow), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_arrow, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Mathematical Transformation

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Transformation

Matrix P converts pirate coordinates to standard ones.
P-inverse performs the reverse translation back to the pirate.
The formula [v]_standard equals P times [v]_new.
This math keeps everyone's perspective perfectly aligned.

Substitute matrix P and vector [1, 1] into the matrix multiplication.
Calculate the product: [2*1 + -1*1, 1*1 + 1*1] resulting in [1, 2].

        # 5. Transformation: Change of Basis
        # New basis vectors: b1 = [1, 0.5], b2 = [0.5, 1]
        basis_change_matrix = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]
        
        new_plane = plane.copy().apply_matrix(basis_change_matrix)
        new_plane.set_color(BLUE)
        
        # New coordinates in basis B: v = [0.66, 0.66] roughly, 
        # but for clarity let's show the transformation of the grid
        new_label = MathTex(
            r"\vec{v} = \begin{bmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{bmatrix}_B", 
            color=BLUE, 
            font_size=30
        )
        self.place_at_grid(new_label, "A4")

        basis_text = Text("Basis Changed", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_text, "A6")

        self.play(
            Transform(plane, new_plane),
            Transform(coords_label, new_label),
            FadeIn(basis_text),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        # 6. Final Highlight
        # Keep the vector fixed in physical space while the grid moves underneath it
        self.play(
            Indicate(vec_v, color=WHITE),
            self.lecture[6:].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix
outline.content: Explain how to bridge the two worlds. The 'Change of Basis Matrix' (P) is simply a matrix where the columns are the coordinates of the NEW basis vectors (b1, b2) written in terms of the OLD basis.
outline.example: If the Pirate's first basis vector is [2, 1] in our standard view, and their second is [-1, 1], the transition matrix P is [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. This matrix 'speaks' both languages.

storyboard.title: The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix
lecture_lines: Matrix P bridges these two different coordinate worlds.
Its columns are new basis vectors in standard terms.
This matrix serves as a translation manual between grids.
animations: Display standard basis vectors i (#0000FF) and j (#00FF00) as reference.
Plot Pirate's basis vectors b1 (#FFA500) at [2, 1] and b2 (#00FFFF) at [-1, 1].
Highlight the standard coordinates of b1 and b2 with dashed lines.
Form matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] by placing b1 and b2 as columns.
Label the columns of P as 'b1' and 'b2' in their respective colors.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Translation Manual: The Change of Basis Matrix"
        lines = [
            "Matrix P bridges these two different coordinate worlds.",
            "Its columns are new basis vectors in standard terms.",
            "This matrix serves as a translation manual between grids."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_B1 = "#FFA500"
        COLOR_B2 = "#00FFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Axes for the vectors
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_C},
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'F4')
        
        # Standard basis vectors
        vec_i = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_I)
        vec_j = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_J)
        
        lbl_i = MathTex("i", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20).next_to(vec_i.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        lbl_j = MathTex("j", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20).next_to(vec_j.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Pirate basis vectors
        vec_b1 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_B1)
        vec_b2 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_B2)
        
        lbl_b1 = MathTex("b_1", color=COLOR_B1, font_size=20).next_to(vec_b1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        lbl_b2 = MathTex("b_2", color=COLOR_B2, font_size=20).next_to(vec_b2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(vec_i), Create(vec_j), Write(lbl_i), Write(lbl_j))
        self.play(Create(vec_b1), Create(vec_b2), Write(lbl_b1), Write(lbl_b2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dashed lines for b1 standard coordinates (2, 1)
        dash_b1_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(2, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), color=COLOR_B1)
        dash_b1_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(2, 1), color=COLOR_B1)
        
        # Dashed lines for b2 standard coordinates (-1, 1)
        dash_b2_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(-1, 0), axes.c2p(-1, 1), color=COLOR_B2)
        dash_b2_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 1), axes.c2p(-1, 1), color=COLOR_B2)
        
        self.play(Create(dash_b1_x), Create(dash_b1_y))
        self.play(Create(dash_b2_x), Create(dash_b2_y))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Matrix P construction
        # Matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        matrix_p = Matrix(
            [[2, -1], [1, 1]],
            left_bracket="[",
            right_bracket="]",
            element_to_mobject_config={"font_size": 28}
        )
        # Color columns
        matrix_p.get_columns()[0].set_color(COLOR_B1)
        matrix_p.get_columns()[1].set_color(COLOR_B2)
        
        # Matrix Label
        p_label = MathTex("P = ", font_size=28)
        p_group = VGroup(p_label, matrix_p).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Column labels
        b1_col_lbl = MathTex("b_1", color=COLOR_B1, font_size=20)
        b2_col_lbl = MathTex("b_2", color=COLOR_B2, font_size=20)
        
        # Use B002 to center the matrix group
        self.place_in_area(p_group, 'B5', 'D6', scale_factor=0.9)
        # Anchor column labels relative to the matrix
        b1_col_lbl.next_to(matrix_p.get_columns()[0], UP, buff=0.2)
        b2_col_lbl.next_to(matrix_p.get_columns()[1], UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(p_group))
        self.play(Write(b1_col_lbl), Write(b2_col_lbl))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Visualizing a New Basis"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Let's define a new basis using vectors b1 and b2.",
            "- These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.",
            "- The space remains fixed while our ruler changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from the prompt/storyboard
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        GREY = "#696969"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # 1. Dim grey (#696969) standard grid background.
        # Adjusted position and scale per Issue 30
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, 'A3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        origin = std_grid.get_origin()
        
        self.play(Create(std_grid))
        
        # 2. Basis vectors b1 (orange #FFA500), b2 (cyan #00FFFF) from origin.
        # Use coordinates relative to the standard grid's unit size
        b1_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(1.5, 0.5)
        b2_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(0.5, 1.5)
        
        b1_arrow = Arrow(origin, b1_target, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(origin, b2_target, buff=0, color=CYAN)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1", color=ORANGE).scale(0.8)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2", color=CYAN).scale(0.8)
        
        # Position labels near the vector heads
        b1_label.next_to(b1_arrow.get_end(), RIGHT + DOWN, buff=0.1)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT + UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_arrow), Write(b1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b2_arrow), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # 3. New skewed grid using orange and cyan lines.
        # Basis matrix
        matrix = [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]
        
        skewed_grid = VGroup()
        # Create a set of grid lines that will be transformed
        # Vertical lines (transformed unit x steps)
        for x in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([x, -3, 0]), np.array([x, 3, 0]), color=ORANGE, stroke_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
        # Horizontal lines (transformed unit y steps)
        for y in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([-3, y, 0]), np.array([3, y, 0]), color=CYAN, stroke_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
            
        # Apply the basis transformation
        skewed_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        # Adjusted position and scale per Issue 31
        self.place_in_area(skewed_grid, 'A3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Show a fixed vector v = [2, 2] in standard coordinates
        v_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(2, 2)
        v_arrow = Arrow(origin, v_target, buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).scale(0.9)
        v_label.next_to(v_arrow.get_end(), UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_arrow, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Visualizing a New Basis"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Let's define a new basis using vectors b1 and b2.",
            "- These vectors form a squashed and rotated grid.",
            "- The space remains fixed while our ruler changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from the prompt/storyboard
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        GREY = "#696969"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # 1. Dim grey (#696969) standard grid background.
        # Adjusted position and scale per Issue 30
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, 'A3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        origin = std_grid.get_origin()
        
        self.play(Create(std_grid))
        
        # 2. Basis vectors b1 (orange #FFA500), b2 (cyan #00FFFF) from origin.
        # Use coordinates relative to the standard grid's unit size
        b1_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(1.5, 0.5)
        b2_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(0.5, 1.5)
        
        b1_arrow = Arrow(origin, b1_target, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(origin, b2_target, buff=0, color=CYAN)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1", color=ORANGE).scale(0.8)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2", color=CYAN).scale(0.8)
        
        # Position labels near the vector heads
        b1_label.next_to(b1_arrow.get_end(), RIGHT + DOWN, buff=0.1)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_arrow.get_end(), LEFT + UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(b1_arrow), Write(b1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b2_arrow), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # 3. New skewed grid using orange and cyan lines.
        # Basis matrix
        matrix = [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]
        
        skewed_grid = VGroup()
        # Create a set of grid lines that will be transformed
        # Vertical lines (transformed unit x steps)
        for x in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([x, -3, 0]), np.array([x, 3, 0]), color=ORANGE, stroke_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
        # Horizontal lines (transformed unit y steps)
        for y in range(-3, 4):
            l = Line(np.array([-3, y, 0]), np.array([3, y, 0]), color=CYAN, stroke_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=2)
            skewed_grid.add(l)
            
        # Apply the basis transformation
        skewed_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        # Adjusted position and scale per Issue 31
        self.place_in_area(skewed_grid, 'A3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Show a fixed vector v = [2, 2] in standard coordinates
        v_target = std_grid.coords_to_point(2, 2)
        v_arrow = Arrow(origin, v_target, buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).scale(0.9)
        v_label.next_to(v_arrow.get_end(), UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_arrow, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Introduction: The Perspective Problem"
        lines = [
            "One point can have many different coordinate descriptions.",
            "An explorer uses a standard North-East grid.",
            "A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid.",
            "They see the same \"X\" using different numbers.",
            "Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_STANDARD = WHITE
        COLOR_PIRATE = YELLOW
        COLOR_X = RED
        
        # Core positions in the 6x6 system
        origin_pos = self.grid['D2']
        x_pos = self.grid['B5']  # Point "X" at (3, 2) relative to D2
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "One point can have many different coordinate descriptions."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        
        # Draw a red 'X'
        point_x = Cross(stroke_width=6).scale(0.2).set_color(COLOR_X)
        point_x.move_to(x_pos)

            y_length=5
        )
        # Shift origin to D2
        standard_grid.shift(origin_pos - standard_grid.get_origin())
        
        explorer_label = Text("Explorer", font_size=24, color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        # Fixed: Move from A1 to A2 per VideoCritic (Issue 27)
        self.place_at_grid(explorer_label, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(standard_grid), Write(explorer_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # "A pirate uses a tilted treasure map grid."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PIRATE))
        
        # Tilted yellow grid
        pirate_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_PIRATE, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},

            y_length=5
        )

        self.play(Create(pirate_grid), Write(pirate_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "They see the same \"X\" using different numbers."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_X))
        
        # Standard projection lines (Horizontal/Vertical)
        std_proj_x = DashedLine(x_pos, [x_pos[0], origin_pos[1], 0], color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        std_proj_y = DashedLine(x_pos, [origin_pos[0], x_pos[1], 0], color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        
        # Pirate projection lines (Along basis vectors)
        # Basis vectors: b1 = [1.2, 0.5], b2 = [-0.3, 1.1]
        p_b1 = np.array([1.2, 0.5, 0])
        p_b2 = np.array([-0.3, 1.1, 0])
        c1, c2 = 2.65, 0.61 # Derived coefficients for (3,2) in Pirate basis
        
        pirate_proj_1 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c1*p_b1, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        pirate_proj_2 = DashedLine(x_pos, origin_pos + c2*p_b2, color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        self.play(Create(std_proj_x), Create(std_proj_y))
        self.play(Create(pirate_proj_1), Create(pirate_proj_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Coordinates depend entirely on your chosen basis."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        std_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Standard: } \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_STANDARD)
        pirate_coords = MathTex(r"\text{Pirate: } \begin{bmatrix} 2.65 \\ 0.61 \end{bmatrix}", color=COLOR_PIRATE)
        
        # Fixed: Move from F row to E row per VideoCritic (Issue 29)
        self.place_in_area(std_coords, 'E1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(pirate_coords, 'E4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Write(std_coords), Write(pirate_coords))
        self.wait(2)

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
